KEY.thesis_one_line: Regional bank whose interest income has grown for eight straight quarters since a 2024 balance-sheet reset backed by a $2.8 billion Scotiabank investment.
KEY.confidence_in_thesis: med - the eight-quarter NII uptrend and the Scotiabank capital terms are directly confirmed in primary filings, but the ~9%/yr implied growth relies on that trend continuing, which is not yet tested across a full rate/credit cycle
kill_criteria: Net interest income (consolidated, quarterly) falls quarter-over-quarter for two consecutive quarters (vs. eight straight quarters of increases through Q2 2026)
CET1 ratio (KeyCorp, consolidated) falls below 9.5% (vs. 11.17% now and a 7.70% regulatory minimum+buffer)
Net charge-offs (consolidated, quarterly) exceed 75bps for two consecutive quarters (vs. 42bps now)
Diluted EPS growth YoY turns negative for two consecutive quarters (excluding the already-disclosed Q3 2024 repositioning loss)
Scotiabank reduces its stake below 5% or the board-representation/standstill terms are renegotiated adversely
key_adverse_facts: Q3 2024 net loss of $410M (EPS -$0.47) was a deliberate securities-portfolio repositioning loss taken alongside the Scotiabank capital raise - large and real, even though the resulting NII uptrend that followed is the basis for the bull case
ROE (b1, 10.3%) is only middling for a regional bank; profitability recovery is real but not yet best-in-class
$2.5bn of preferred stock (Series D-H, 5.0-6.2% coupons) sits senior to common dividends
Regional-bank commercial real estate exposure is an industry-wide risk not independently stress-tested here at standard depth

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for KEY (bank valuation methodology not run by V1 at this ticker). My own reverse DCF implies ~9%/yr 10-year EPS growth at the $20.61 close, versus my evidence-based base case of 7-8%/yr (continuation of the confirmed NII-repricing trend before normalizing) - close to, and arguably marginally above, base, so this is priced as a fair, not a bargain, recovery story.

KEY.scenario_basis: Starting point NTM consensus non-GAAP EPS ~$2.06 (d4 eps_ntm) and current dividend $0.205/qtr ($0.82/yr, ~4.0% yield) at the $20.61 close. Bear: NIM/credit cycle turns unfavorably, EPS growth stalls at 2-4%/yr, multiple compresses toward 8x forward P/E. Base: NII-repricing tailwind continues for 1-2 more years then normalizes (~7-8%/yr EPS growth), multiple holds near today's 9.65x forward, dividend continues at ~4% yield. Bull: NIM expansion and Scotiabank-partnership synergies sustain 10-12%/yr EPS growth, multiple re-rates toward 12x, buybacks continue at the current aggressive pace.

MDT.thesis_one_line: Global medical-device maker whose growth has genuinely reaccelerated and guidance has been raised twice running, clouded by two live, unresolved court-verdict overhangs.
MDT.confidence_in_thesis: high - the guidance-raise track record and both litigation overhangs are directly confirmed and dated in the same primary-source 10-Q and earnings-release exhibits
kill_criteria: FY27 organic revenue growth guidance is cut below the current 7.25%-7.75% range (vs. two consecutive raises through Q1 FY27)
Net debt/EBITDA (consolidated) rises above 3.0x (vs. approximately 1.9x now)
The Applied Medical antitrust verdict is upheld on appeal at $500M or more (post-trebling/fees) without a stay
Hernia-mesh MDL plaintiff count exceeds 20,000 or a second bellwether verdict exceeds $50M
GAAP-to-non-GAAP EPS gap widens beyond 30% of GAAP EPS for two consecutive quarters (Q1 FY27 gap already 27%)
key_adverse_facts: Applied Medical antitrust jury verdict (2026-02-05): $382M in damages, automatically trebled by law (potential ~$1.15bn exposure before fees/injunctive relief sought), unaccrued, under appeal
Hernia mesh MDL: ~10,500 plaintiffs as of 2026-08-05; first bellwether verdict $88M against Medtronic (2026-08-04), unaccrued, under challenge
Ongoing, disclosed SEC/DOJ anti-corruption dialogue regarding certain international-market practices (no liability recorded, no charges disclosed)
SBC rose from $86M to $125M year-over-year in the most recent quarter (+45%), worth monitoring though still small relative to revenue

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for MDT (not run by V1 at this ticker). My own reverse DCF implies ~6.7%/yr 10-year non-GAAP EPS growth at the $88.64 close, which sits within (at the low end of) my evidence-based base case of 6-8%/yr - the market is not paying for materially more growth than the company's own newly-raised FY27 guidance already implies.

MDT.scenario_basis: Starting point FY27 non-GAAP diluted EPS guidance midpoint ~$5.97 and current dividend $2.88/yr (3.25% yield) at the $88.64 close, forward P/E 14.4x. Bear: growth reverts to Medtronic's pre-2026 mid-single-digit historical norm and one or both litigation overhangs cost real cash, multiple compresses toward 13x. Base: FY27 guided growth trajectory (7-8%/yr EPS) continues 2-3 more years then moderates, multiple holds near 14-15x, dividend continues at ~3.25% yield. Bull: new product cycles (cardiac ablation, Hugo, Affera/Sphere-9) sustain high-single-to-low-double-digit growth, both litigation items resolve for immaterial amounts, multiple re-rates toward 16-17x.

MCHP.thesis_one_line: Analog-chip maker in a real, confirmed cyclical recovery from a severe inventory correction, but priced for growth above even a bullish decade, on a more levered balance sheet than the headline ratio shows.
MCHP.horizon: n/a - not held; would revisit on a lower entry price or faster deleveraging
MCHP.confidence_in_thesis: high - the guidance-beat streak, gross-margin recovery and $1.485bn mandatory convertible preferred are all directly confirmed in primary-source filings; the reverse-DCF conclusion is the analyst's own model, clearly labelled as such
kill_criteria: Quarterly net sales sequential growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters (vs. five straight quarters of sequential growth through Q1 FY27)
Net debt/EBITDA (including the mandatory convertible preferred as debt-like) fails to fall below 4.0x within four quarters (vs. approximately 4.4x now)
Gross margin (GAAP, consolidated) falls back below 58% for two consecutive quarters (vs. 63.2% now)
A guidance miss (actual net sales below the low end of the company's own guided range) for the first time in the last six quarters
The company suspends or cuts the common dividend (currently $0.455/share, unchanged through the entire review period)
key_adverse_facts: Net debt/EBITDA is 3.4x on the headline consolidated basis (confirming the triage's own flag) and approximately 4.4x once the $1.485bn, 7.50%-coupon mandatory convertible preferred stock (issued 2025-03-25) is counted as debt-like capital

The triage's cited red flag of a '2024 dividend cut' is not supported by any of five quarterly earnings releases reviewed (Nov 2024 - Aug 2026); the common dividend has been held flat at $0.455/share throughout, described as a 'record' dividend at points - the real capital-structure stress event was the mandatory convertible preferred raise, not a dividend cut
Beta 1.74 (high) reflects genuine cyclicality; Microchip has been through at least two severe down-cycles in the past decade
Common share buybacks have been paused/minimal since FY25 while the company prioritizes deleveraging
data_conflicts: Triage (Q12_triage.json) cited a '2024 dividend cut' as a red flag; primary-source earnings releases from Q2 FY25 (Nov 2024) through Q1 FY27 (Aug 2026) show the common dividend held flat at $0.455/share throughout, with no cut evidenced in any filing reviewed - the triage appears to have conflated this with the March 2025 mandatory convertible preferred stock raise, which is the real, material capital-structure event

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for MCHP (not run by V1 at this ticker). My own reverse DCF implies ~12.5%/yr 10-year non-GAAP EPS growth at the $78.69 close, above my evidence-based base case of 8-9%/yr (a 2-3 year cyclical catch-up toward the prior FY23 peak followed by normalization to Microchip's historical structural growth rate) and near the top of my own bull case (13-15%/yr) - the price already requires close to a bull outcome sustained for a full decade, which is the basis for the WATCH verdict under the wave-4 rule that implied growth above base means WATCH, not INCLUDE.

MCHP.scenario_basis: Starting point NTM consensus non-GAAP EPS ~$4.10 (d4 eps_ntm) and current dividend $1.82/yr (~2.3% yield) at the $78.69 close, NTM P/E 19.2x. Bear: recovery stalls or a fresh semis down-cycle hits, EPS stays near $3.50 in 3 years, multiple compresses to 14x. Base: cyclical recovery continues moderately, EPS reaches ~$4.80-5.00 in 3 years, multiple normalizes toward 16x (below today's 19.2x), roughly offsetting the EPS gain. Bull: recovery fully plays out, EPS reaches ~$6.00 in 3 years, multiple holds near 20x.
